{"content":"## Creating a Google Cloud Compute Engine Instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

Below is a complete example of how to create a Compute Engine instance via the REST API (or `curl`) that includes an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from the official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.

> **Prerequisites**
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with the **Compute Engine API** enabled.
> * You must have a **service account** with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent) and the `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` role to act as the instance's service account.
> * The project must have a **GPU quota** for the `nvidia-tesla-a6000` accelerator in the chosen zone.
> * The instance will automatically install the NVIDIA GPU driver via a startup script (see below).

### 1. Define Variables

| Variable | Example | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `PROJECT_ID` | `my-gcp-project` | Your GCP project ID |
| `ZONE` | `us-central1-a` | The zone where the instance will be created |
| `INSTANCE_NAME` | `rtx-a6000-ubuntu` | Desired instance name |
| `MACHINE_TYPE` | `n1-standard-8` | Machine type (adjust CPU/RAM as needed) |
| `GPU_COUNT` | `1` | Number of RTX A6000 GPUs |
| `IMAGE_FAMILY` | `ubuntu-2004-lts` | Official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family |
| `IMAGE_PROJECT` | `ubuntu-os-cloud` | Project that hosts the Ubuntu image |
| `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` | `my-sa@my-gcp-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com` | Service account for the instance |

### 2. JSON Body for the Instance Creation Request

```json
{
  "name": "${INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "zones/${ZONE}/machineTypes/${MACHINE_TYPE}",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/${IMAGE_PROJECT}/global/images/family/${IMAGE_FAMILY}"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": ${GPU_COUNT}
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL}",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\n# Install NVIDIA driver\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\n# Reboot to load driver (optional)\n# reboot"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **Note**: Replace the `${...}` placeholders with your actual values.

### 3. `curl` Command to Invoke the REST API

```bash
# Authenticate and obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Make the POST request
curl \n  -X POST \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d @instance.json \n  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

* `instance.json` should contain the JSON body from step 2.

### 4. Verify Instance Creation

After the request completes, you can verify the instance via the console or by running:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe ${INSTANCE_NAME} --zone=${ZONE}
```

You should see the `guestAccelerators` section listing the RTX A6000 GPU and the `metadata` section containing the startup script.

### 5. Connecting to the Instance

Once the instance is running, SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh ${INSTANCE_NAME} --zone=${ZONE}
```

Verify the GPU is recognized:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed.

---

#### Alternative: Using `gcloud` CLI Directly

If you prefer not to use the REST API, the same instance can be created with a single `gcloud` command:

```bash
gcloud compute instances create ${INSTANCE_NAME} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=${MACHINE_TYPE} \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=${GPU_COUNT} \
  --image-family=${IMAGE_FAMILY} \
  --image-project=${IMAGE_PROJECT} \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --service-account=${SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL} \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata=startup-script='#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535'
```

This command achieves the same result but uses the higher‑level `gcloud` abstraction.

---

**Important**: GPU instances incur additional costs. Ensure you understand the pricing for the RTX A6000 in your chosen zone.

"},"filename":"create-rtx-a6000-instance.md"}
